questions.q: What question does an architecture diagram answer, as distinct from a runbook?
options: What the environment is and how it's laid out — VNets/VPCs, subnets, tiers, and connections
Who is on call this week
How to restart a specific service
Where billing alerts are configured
questions.explain: The diagram is the visual 'what' — the shape and layout of the environment, not operating instructions.

questions.q: What does a runbook cover that an architecture diagram does not?
options: Common operational tasks, who to contact, and where logs live
The exact CIDR ranges of every subnet
A list of every resource's creation date
The company's org chart
questions.explain: A runbook is the practical, step-by-step reference for operating and troubleshooting the environment day to day.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why are an architecture diagram and a runbook written together rather than as separate, unrelated projects?
options: Because the diagram gives the runbook its context — runbook steps like 'check web-vm-01/02/03' only make sense with the diagram's layout behind them
Because most documentation tools require both files to be in one folder
Because the runbook is simply a copy of the diagram in text form
There is no real reason — it's just a team preference
questions.explain: A runbook step naming specific VMs or subnets is far more usable when the reader can see those names placed on the diagram.

questions.q: In the example runbook entry for an unresponsive web tier, what does step 2 ('Connect via bastion-vm') rely on to be clear?
options: The diagram showing the Management subnet and how it reaches the Web Tier
A separate billing report
Nothing — the step is self-explanatory without any other document
The monitoring dashboard's uptime percentage
questions.explain: Step 2 points back at the diagram's Management subnet, the same way step 1 points at the Web Tier — the runbook leans on the diagram throughout.

questions.q: What happens when a runbook exists but no architecture diagram does?
options: An instruction like 'restart the web tier' leaves the reader no way to know which specific resources that means or how they connect
Nothing changes — the runbook works exactly the same either way
The runbook automatically generates a diagram from its steps
Monitoring tools refuse to alert without a diagram present
questions.explain: Without the diagram's context, runbook instructions are technically correct but slow to use, since the reader has no mental map of what they're operating.
